Why You Got That Error
That json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 90131 happened for a simple reason:

When you stopped/killed the previous search in PowerShell (Ctrl+C or closing the window), Python was in the middle of writing one of the cached variant JSON files to disk (with open(path, "w") as f: json.dump(...)), leaving a half-written, truncated file at character 90,130.
When you started the new run, supersearch_turbo.py saw that .json file in data/supersearch/cache/, tried to load it with json.load(f), and crashed because the JSON was incomplete.
How We Permanently Fixed It
I have updated both scripts/supersearch_turbo.py and scripts/route_compiler_v19.py with self-healing cache protection:

Every single cache load is now wrapped in a try...except Exception: block.
If any cached .json file is truncated, corrupted, or fails to parse for any reason, the script now automatically deletes the broken cache file (os.remove) and recompiles it cleanly from scratch without crashing.
What to Run Now on Your Desktop PC
When you download the fresh folder (with the updated route_compiler_v19.py and supersearch_turbo.py), the script will automatically delete that broken cache file for you.

If you want to be 100% sure your local cache directory is clean before launching, you can run this in PowerShell on one line:

PowerShell

Remove-Item -Recurse -Force data\supersearch\cache, data\supersearch\cache_records -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; python scripts\supersearch_turbo.py --seeds 1,2,3 --opps all --finalists 20 --procs 8 --build-agent
(Or if using the wrapper: Remove-Item -Recurse -Force data\supersearch\cache, data\supersearch\cache_records -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; .\scripts\turbo.ps1 -Seeds "1,2,3" -Opps all -Finalists 20 -Procs 8 -BuildAgent)

Your 8-core Ryzen will now sail through cleanly without ever choking on a corrupted cache file!

Official per-turn timeout from engine JSON: actTimeout: 1.
SELL draws only from private["shed"], never carried inventory.

Planting day counts as unwatered:
new plant consecutive_unwatered = 1

WHEAT crop config from engine:
Python

"WHEAT": {"seed": 10, "first_yield_day": 2, "max_yield_day": 4, "interval": 0, "max_yield": 6, "ongoing": False}
Critical yield mechanic discovered:
Non-ongoing crops (WHEAT/CARROT) do not simply auto-maximize yield over time.
During maturity window, WATER increases yield:
Python

if not crop_data["ongoing"]:
    age_days = day - tile["planted_day"]
    window_start = (crop_data["max_yield_day"] + 1) // 2
    if window_start <= age_days <= crop_data["max_yield_day"]:
        bonus = 2 if tile["fertilized_until_day"] >= day else 1
        tile["yield_units"] = min(crop_data["max_yield"], tile["yield_units"] + bonus)
Therefore blindly replacing late WATER with HARVEST loses money because late water boosts WHEAT yield before harvest.

restart_turbo.ps1
PLAIN
# restart_turbo.ps1 — preserve data, wipe OLD cartesian cache, launch v20.
#   .\scripts\restart_turbo.ps1
# Ctrl+C any old run first.

param(
    [string]$Seeds = "1,2,3",
    [string]$Opps = "all",
    [int]$Finalists = 20,
    [int]$Procs = 8,
    [switch]$BuildAgent
)

$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
Set-Location $root

Write-Host "=== restart_turbo v20 ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan

$ledger = "data\supersearch\ledger_turbo.jsonl"
if (Test-Path $ledger) {
    $stamp = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd_HHmmss"
    $dst = "data\supersearch\ledger_turbo_$stamp.jsonl"
    Copy-Item $ledger $dst
    Write-Host "Preserved old ledger -> $dst" -ForegroundColor Green
} else {
    Write-Host "No old ledger found." -ForegroundColor Yellow
}

foreach ($c in @("data\supersearch\cache", "data\supersearch\cache_records")) {
    if (Test-Path $c) {
        Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $c
        Write-Host "Removed old cache: $c" -ForegroundColor Green
    }
}

$cmd = @(
    "scripts\supersearch_turbo.py",
    "--seeds", $Seeds,
    "--opps", $Opps,
    "--finalists", "$Finalists",
    "--procs", "$Procs",
    "--mode", "surgical",
    "--fresh"
)
if ($BuildAgent) { $cmd += "--build-agent" }

Write-Host "Launching: python $cmd" -ForegroundColor Cyan
python @cmd
Open
turbo.ps1
PLAIN
# turbo.ps1 — run the v20 SURGICAL supersearch.
#
#   cd Z:\Kaggle\Works\kaggriculture
#   .\scripts\turbo.ps1 -Seeds "1,2,3" -Opps all -Finalists 20 -Procs 8 -BuildAgent
#
# First run after downloading this folder, wipe the old cartesian cache:
#   Remove-Item -Recurse -Force data\supersearch\cache, data\supersearch\cache_records -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; .\scripts\turbo.ps1 -Seeds "1,2,3" -Opps all -Finalists 20 -Procs 8 -BuildAgent
#
# Resume after a reboot: run the same command. Ledger is kept. Use -Fresh to start over (ledger is backed up first).

param(
    [string]$Seeds = "1,2,3",
    [string]$GateSeeds = "1",
    [string]$Opps = "all",
    [string]$Dims = "",
    [string]$Mode = "surgical",
    [int]$Procs = 8,
    [int]$Finalists = 20,
    [int]$Threshold = 200,
    [switch]$BuildAgent,
    [switch]$Fresh
)

$cmd = @(
    "scripts\supersearch_turbo.py",
    "--seeds", $Seeds,
    "--gate-seeds", $GateSeeds,
    "--opps", $Opps,
    "--mode", $Mode,
    "--finalists", "$Finalists",
    "--threshold", "$Threshold",
    "--procs", "$Procs"
)
if ($Dims)      { $cmd += "--dims"; $cmd += $Dims }
if ($BuildAgent) { $cmd += "--build-agent" }
if ($Fresh)      { $cmd += "--fresh" }

Write-Host "Running: python $cmd"
python @cmd
Open

2
Windows killed the run. All 8 workers tried to write the same base-record file at once (rec_3a216346efdc0c91_seat0.json). Linux allows that replace. Windows returns Access is denied.

Fixed:

File lock — only one process writes that shared record. Everyone else waits and loads it.
Retry on WinError 5 — if Defender or another worker has the file, it backs off instead of crashing.
Pre-warm — main process writes both seat records before the 8 workers start.
A worker error is logged and skipped. It no longer kills the whole pool.
Leftover .tmp / .lock files from the crash are cleaned on startup.
Download the folder again and run the same command. Resume is on, so it will skip anything already in the ledger.

PowerShell

python scripts\supersearch_turbo.py --seeds 1,2,3 --opps all --finalists 20 --procs 8 --build-agent
You should see pre-warming base records then base records ready before the variant lines start. If a single variant hits a Windows lock it will print ERROR and keep going.

What each lever actually did
idle=2 (step onto a neighbor plant) — killed everything. All 1,020 of those dropped to $88k–$130k. Walking off the tape desyncs the route. Dead. Never use it.

idle=1 (WATER if already standing on a plant) — no-op. Same money, same 7 leftovers. Workers almost never PASS on a dry crop.

leftover harvest h1/h2 — no-op. Those 7 day-26 wheat sit at row 8–9. Nobody PASSes on those tiles, so a “if you’re already there, harvest” patch never fires. Need a real walk, not a PASS swap.

feed stagger — keepers at $167,781 (−$197) and a worse gate (−2.2k / −5.1k). Cow math costs more than it saves vs v18/tetsu.

feed buffer +5 — no reward change. Extra wheat sat unused.

odd-day splice (the 52-vs-62 idea) — when it didn’t also use idle=2, money stayed $167,978 and the gate stayed −762. Recompiling day 11/13/15/17 did not add harvestable yield on this tape.

Every keeper was 1-1 vs v18, 0-2 vs tetsu. Same as base.

What this means
Two full searches now (10,800 coarse + 3,060 surgical) have both said the same thing: you cannot beat this tape by mutating crops, hires, animals, water policy, or splicing days. The v18 route is locally maxed. Another overnight grid of the same knobs will waste the same CPU.

The leftover $560 and the tetsu/seat1 hole are still real. They need one-off planners, not a 3,000-variant cartesian:

A day-28/29 walker that actually paths a worker to those 7 wheat, waters in the yield window, harvests, and gets back to the shed.
A tetsu/seat1 counter that keys off their visible farm, not a new tape.
I can build those next as small targeted scripts you run locally (minutes, not hours). Say the word. Until then, keep HI_AgriBot_v18 live.

three_fer.ps1
PLAIN
# three_fer.ps1 — leftover walker + tetsu/seat1 counter + distinctive path.
#
#   cd Z:\Kaggle\Works\kaggriculture
#   .\scripts\three_fer.ps1 -Seeds "1,2,3" -Procs 8
#   .\scripts\three_fer.ps1 -DiagnoseOnly
#   .\scripts\three_fer.ps1 -Quick -Procs 8
#   .\scripts\three_fer.ps1 -Seeds "1,2,3" -Procs 8 -BuildAgent
#
# NOT a cartesian. ~20 local one-offs. Minutes on a 3700X.
# Do NOT ship unless the report says SHIP=YES. Keep HI_AgriBot_v18 live.

param(
    [string]$Seeds = "1,2,3",
    [string]$GateSeeds = "1,2,3",
    [int]$Procs = 8,
    [switch]$DiagnoseOnly,
    [switch]$Quick,
    [switch]$BuildAgent
)

$cmd = @(
    "scripts\three_fer.py",
    "--seeds", $Seeds,
    "--gate-seeds", $GateSeeds,
    "--procs", "$Procs"
)
if ($DiagnoseOnly) { $cmd += "--diagnose-only" }
if ($Quick)        { $cmd += "--quick" }
if ($BuildAgent)   { $cmd += "--build-agent" }

Write-Host "Running: python $cmd"
python @cmd
Open

three_fer.py
PYTHON
Three-fer is ready. Not another cartesian — 36 local one-offs, about 8–10 minutes on the 3700X (or 2 minutes with -Quick).

Keep HI_AgriBot_v18 live. Do not ship unless data/three_fer/report.json says SHIP=YES.

What it actually does
1. Leftover walker (the real walk)
Old h1/h2 was a no-op: it only swapped PASS→HARVEST if a worker was already standing on the wheat, and they never are. This one:

picks the idlest non-tender worker(s) on day 27/28
walks them to the leftover wheat (simulated positions, not the stale visits map)
WATER on day 28 (yield), HARVEST on day 29
turns for home with enough steps left so the step-718 terminal sweep can bank it
2. Tetsu / seat1 counter (visible farm only)
Tetsu is a single-tape bot. Detector keys off the public farm: crop count, 3-quad / no SE, animal band, wheat mix, and plant-tile Jaccard vs our own layout. High Jaccard = our mirror (do nothing). Low Jaccard + route-bot production = tetsu. Then, legally:

convert existing PLANT STRAWBERRY → TOMATO under glut
skip late BUY_ANIMAL on seat1 when the herd is already full
No cloning, no sabotage, no runtime path rewrite.

3. Distinctive path (same result, different walk)
Equivalent-length Manhattan rewrite of MOVE stretches (x-first / y-first / zig / anti-greedy). Same anchors, same arrival times, different staircase. Days 28–29 left for the walker. This is the “not a Yubo/Gbining copy” lever — offline only, keep-gated.

Run it
PowerShell

cd Z:\Kaggle\Works\kaggriculture
python scripts\three_fer.py --self-test
.\scripts\three_fer.ps1 -DiagnoseOnly
.\scripts\three_fer.ps1 -Quick -Procs 8
.\scripts\three_fer.ps1 -Seeds "1,2,3" -Procs 8
-BuildAgent is a no-op unless something ships. Outputs: data/three_fer/diagnose.json, ledger.jsonl, report.json.

Ship gate unchanged: seed1 seat0 vs PASS ≥ $167,978, animals ≥ 13, 0 losses vs v18 on seeds 1–3 both seats.

Other ideas (not in this script)
Seat1 opening splice (days 0–3 only) — the ~$12k seat1 gap is structural. Leftover wheat cannot fix it.
(7,4) cow: one reserved feeder, not global feed_repair (that lost $1k–$11k).
Harvest leftovers on day 27 if yield_units > 0 — more time to walk home. w1d27 already tries a version of this.
Tetsu straw preemption on day 17/23 only — full clone-preempt died when it touched days 0–11.
Do not rerun crop/hire/animal/water/splice grids. Two full searches said local max.
Upload data/three_fer/ when it finishes and I’ll read the leftover tiles, Jaccard, and whether anything actually cleared the gate.
